title: Elastic overlay constraining and table gesture handoff
creator: Asha Patel
description: Polish console pages so overlays (filters, rollouts flyouts, cost breakdown panels) behave predictably across breakpoints and browsers when stacked on top of scrollable tables and charts. Focus areas: elastic overlay sizing to avoid obscuring important table columns on small viewports, reliable gesture handoff on touch devices (capture vs. pass-through), and consistent clipping/overflow behavior for canvas-based charts (Chart.js/D3) inside modals. Work includes prototypes, cross-browser QA notes, and an accessibility pass for keyboard and screen-reader interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Overlay components (filter drawer, rollout details panel, cost breakdown modal) do not permanently obscure primary table columns at widths >= 320px; critical columns remain visible or collapsible with a clear affordance

Touch gesture handoff is deterministic: dragging within an overlay drains to overlay scroll if content overflows, otherwise the gesture passes to underlying table/chart scroll. Verified on iOS Safari and Chrome for Android
Modal stacking/z-index rules prevent visual clipping of chart tooltips and legend overlays when multiple overlays are open
No regressions in keyboard navigation: tab order is preserved, focus trap rules exist for modals, and escape closes overlays consistently
Cross-browser rendering fixes applied for Safari pointer capture / overscroll-behavior and verified in SauceLabs matrix (Desktop Safari, Mobile Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
prototypes: Chrome DevTools: emulation snapshots included in design folder
comments: 2025-02-11 - Asha: Initial discovery — multiple bug reports from CS showing that the rollout detail panel covers the 'cost per model' column on narrow desktops and iPad in landscape. Logged visuals and started a proto to test overlay min/max widths.

2025-02-14 - Rory: Prototype v1 created in Figma that introduces an 'elastic width' overlay with a collapse handle and a compact column mode for tables. Implement notes: prefer CSS clamp() for overlay width with js fallback for legacy browsers.

2025-02-19 - Mateo (eng): Implement spike — Safari iOS prevents pointer capture when overlay uses transform for animation. Recommending reducing transforms on the overlay container and toggling will-change only during animation to avoid losing touch events.

2025-02-21 - Lin (a11y): Accessibility review — ensure overlay header has role=dialog and aria-modal set; focus trap must land on the first interactive control. Provide an accessible collapse button that announces 'collapse overlay, showing columns X and Y'

2025-02-25 - Samir (QA): Cross-browser matrix run — Chrome/Edge/Firefox pass basic behavior. Failures observed on iOS Safari: overscroll on underlying table when overlay is at top of stack. Workaround tested: overscroll-behavior: contain on overlay and html/body - improved but needs refine for nested scroll containers.
2025-03-01 - PRD link: Confluence draft updated with final acceptance criteria and canary rollout plan for 10% of org via feature flag

2025-03-03 - Rory: Implement branch opened (frontend/overlay-elasticity). Key changes: CSS clamp for width, explicit pointer-events toggling during modal open/close, JS fallback for older Safari that manually call preventDefault on touchstart if overlay scrollHeight > clientHeight.

2025-03-05 - Asha: Design sign-off pending minor visual tweaks to the collapse affordance and tooltip placement; requested Samir to run another round of mobile Safari tests and confirm keyboard focus order in screen-reader mode
acceptance_test_steps: Open console on mobile and desktop widths; open rollout detail overlay and confirm primary table columns are still actionable or a collapsed pattern is offered

On iOS Safari and Android Chrome, with overlay open, perform a vertical swipe inside overlay on both overflowing and non-overflowing content — verify scroll stays inside overlay when content overflows and delegates to background when it does not
Open two stacked overlays and hover/interact with chart tooltips — verify z-index and clipping are handled so tooltips are visible and not cut off
Keyboard test: tab through overlay controls, verify focus trap, then press Escape to close; run with VoiceOver/NVDA and ensure announcements match expectations
Run automated visual diffs for 320, 375, 768, 1024 widths and compare to approved Figma frames
